clue.text: A western criminal, comfortable in retirement and idle

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word for comfortable is read backwards

parts.note: snug means comfortable and cosy
to linger is to idle or loiter

explanation.surface: A Wild West outlaw has settled into a comfortable, lazy retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' reverses the comfortable word; 'idle' looks like describing the criminal but supplies the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunfighter of the American frontier was a typical outlaw of cowboy films.

clue.text: The one making a U-turn can

parts.note: taken as written from the U of U-turn

indicators.note: turning the container word round means the word for can is read backwards

parts.note: a can is a tin

explanation.surface: Someone is making a U-turn with a can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses the can word, and the U is lifted straight from 'U-turn' itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing, a quantity of one.

clue.text: Small plates of fish

parts.note: reads like a menu of little dishes of seafood, but means the protective covering on a fish's skin

explanation.surface: A tapas menu offering small plates of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The skin of a fish is covered with tiny overlapping bony plates.

clue.text: Having no respect for the rogue with debts

parts.note: an imp is a little rogue or mischief-maker
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: A rogue in debt has no respect for anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Impious means lacking reverence, especially towards God.

clue.text: Note a farm animal's pulse

parts.note: G is a musical note
a ram is a male sheep found on farms

explanation.surface: A vet takes a farm animal's pulse and makes a note of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' is not a heartbeat but a bean: gram is a type of legume, as in chickpeas.
explanation.definitionFit: Gram is the chickpea or another edible legume seed, and pulses are legumes.

clue.text: After holiday get foreign currency refund

indicators.note: the currency piece comes after the holiday piece in the answer

parts.note: a rest is a break or holiday
the öre is a small Scandinavian coin

explanation.surface: After a holiday you exchange your leftover foreign currency for a refund.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore money is to give it back, as with a refund.

clue.text: Well-known Greek maids cheer wildly

indicators.note: doing something wildly suggests the letters of the preceding words run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Housemaids cheer wildly for a famous Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Archimedes was the celebrated ancient mathematician of Syracuse.

clue.text: Strip for action!

parts.note: sounds like a call to undress for a fight, but strip is the kit or clothing worn for sport

explanation.surface: A rallying cry to get undressed and ready for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing worn for playing games is what a team calls its strip.

clue.text: Support for cash

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
P stands for penny, a bit of cash

explanation.surface: Someone offers support in exchange for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop is something that holds up or supports.

clue.text: Said unfortunately soft fruit goes off

indicators.note: something going unfortunately goes wrong, so the letters of the word said fall into a new order

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
pears are a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone complains that soft fruit goes rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: To vanish is to go off, out of sight.

clue.text: Restraint shown in maintaining order despite the rowdies

indicators.note: the letters are on display inside the following words, running across despite, the and rowdies

explanation.surface: Police show restraint in keeping order despite the rowdy crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is in 'despiTE THE Rowdies'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tether is a rope that restrains an animal.

clue.text: Age brings back-problems for a scholarly man

parts.note: an era is an age

indicators.note: back makes the word for problems read backwards

parts.note: sums are arithmetic problems

explanation.surface: Old age brings back problems for an academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses SUMS to SMUS. Erasmus was the Dutch Renaissance humanist scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus of Rotterdam was a famous Renaissance humanist and theologian.

clue.text: Currently controlled

parts.note: reads as being in charge at present, but means run by an electric current

explanation.surface: Someone or something is under control at the moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Devices powered by electricity are run by a flowing current.

clue.text: Articles about head-lines read in new Zealand

indicators.note: the two articles go around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
an again, a second indefinite article
a tip is the end or head of something
an ode is a poem, lines of verse

explanation.surface: Articles about newspaper headlines read in New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: The two articles wrap round both inner pieces. Britons call Australia and New Zealand the Antipodes, being on the opposite side of the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: Australians and New Zealanders are from the Antipodes, so things read there are of that region.

clue.text: Covertly attack certain high-fliers

explanation.surface: Sniping at frequent flyers.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoot or criticise from hiding is to snipe; the snipe is also a wading bird that flies high.

clue.text: A goddess merits a break

indicators.note: giving the word merits a break shatters its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A goddess deserves time off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a break' signals the anagram of 'merits', placed after the opening A; 'A goddess' looks like the definition but the A is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemis was the Greek deity of the hunt and the moon.

clue.text: A quarrel — resulting in war or otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged in another way, so the letters of war and or are reordered

explanation.surface: A quarrel that ends up in war, or not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A quarrel' is not a dispute but a crossbow bolt; 'otherwise' rearranges WAR OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel is a short heavy bolt shot from a crossbow, a kind of missile.

clue.text: Poles stoned and sound asleep!

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles
ore is rock or stone that bears metal, so the clue's stoned stands for that stone

explanation.surface: Polish men, high on drugs, are fast asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' are not people from Poland but the compass poles. 'stoned' is used loosely for ORE, mineral-bearing stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Snoring is the noise a sleeper makes while breathing.

clue.text: Tucks into a spread set outside

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go outside, around the single letter
spread out means the letters of set are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tucks into a buffet laid out on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges SET to ETS, and 'outside' puts it around A.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat something is to tuck into it, informally.

clue.text: Lacking work, I'd go with the French

parts.note: the apostrophe is dropped
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Unemployed, the speaker would head off with the French.
explanation.definitionFit: An idle worker is unemployed, without a job to do.

clue.text: Swiss capital — funds intended for a film possibly

indicators.note: a capital is an initial letter, so the opening letter of Swiss is taken

parts.note: a pool is a shared fund of money

explanation.surface: Swiss capital is put into a fund to finance a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' is not Bern but the first letter of 'Swiss'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel onto which camera film is wound is used for cine film.

clue.text: A quarter left with little hesitation due to disparagement

parts.note: S, south, is one of the four quarters of the compass
and means together with
er is a short hesitant sound

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood is left hesitant because of disparaging remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Slander is spoken defamation that disparages someone.

clue.text: He carried a torch for a young member of the chain gang!

parts.note: a link is one member of a chain
a boy is a young male

explanation.surface: A young prisoner in the chain gang carried a torch for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried a torch' suggests unrequited love, but literally a linkboy carried a torch to light the way for people walking the streets at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Before street lighting, a boy hired to carry a flaming torch lit pedestrians home.

clue.text: Help too ill-organised to be really good

indicators.note: badly arranged, so the letters of help and too are reordered

explanation.surface: Help so disorganised it turns out fine after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-organised' rearranges HELP TOO. TOP HOLE is dated British slang for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-hole is old-fashioned upper-class British slang for first-rate.

clue.text: Royal family rolls embellished with gold

parts.note: winds means coils or rolls up
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: The royal family's bread rolls are decorated with gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Windsor is the name of the British royal dynasty.

clue.text: A monk in nothing but a cloak

parts.note: Dom is a title given to some monks
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A monk wears nothing but a cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: A domino is a loose hooded cloak worn with a mask at masquerades.

clue.text: A foreigner returning to assist in a public-house

indicators.note: the reversed piece sits inside the pub word

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word for assist is read backwards

parts.note: aid is another word for assist

explanation.surface: A foreigner coming back to help out at a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns the help word round, and 'in' places that inside the pub; 'A foreigner' is the definition, the pub's 'a' only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from India is a foreign national from a British point of view.

clue.text: A talk written up as a story

indicators.note: in a down clue, writing upwards means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: gas means idle talk or chatter

explanation.surface: A talk written up and published as a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long tale or narrative, originally Norse.

clue.text: Time to accommodate superior, though it gives one the shivers

indicators.note: accommodating someone means taking them in, so the letter goes inside the time word

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
U means upper class, superior

explanation.surface: A long wait for a boss gives someone the shivers.
explanation.walkthrough: U as upper-class is a British convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Ague is a fever with fits of shivering, as in malaria.

clue.text: Men would put this down to attract game

parts.note: to draw is to attract
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: Men would lay down something to attract game when hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put down' looks like hunting game, but the men lower the castle crossing over the moat.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle's raisable crossing over a moat is lowered by the garrison to let people in.

clue.text: Almost all like to amalgamate — such a pity!

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word all loses its final letter

parts.note: as means like

explanation.surface: Nearly everyone wants to merge, more's the pity.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of grief or regret.

clue.text: A person expects no credit for it

definitions.text: A person expects no credit for it

parts.words: A person expects no credit for it
parts.note: reads as a thankless task, but credit is in the money sense: it is paid as cash on the spot

explanation.surface: A thankless deed that nobody will praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Cash paid immediately rather than on account means the seller is giving no credit.
